title: This Lego Spaceship Spins Just Like the Real Thing!
summary: Have you ever built a Lego set that actually moves like a real spaceship? The new Lego Project Hail Mary does exactly that! Based on the movie where Ryan Gosling zooms across space to save Earth, this set has a super cool spinning trick. Inside the display stand, there's a hidden mechanism. When you turn it, the crew part of the ship stretches out and pulls back in. It's just like the centrifugal gravity system from the film — that's the sci-fi way of making artificial gravity by spinning. The whole set has 830 pieces and costs $99.99. It's about the size of a shoebox: 12 inches long, 9.5 inches wide, and 8.5 inches tall. That's smaller than some other big Lego space sets, like the huge NASA rocket. But the spinning feature makes up for it! The build comes in six paper bags. You start with a cute little scene showing the two main characters, Ryland and Rocky, separated by a window — just like when they first meet in the movie. Then you build the stand and the spinning parts. The actual spaceship is built last, with a thruster, three body sections, and a big solar panel array. One awesome thing: no stickers! All the details are printed right on the bricks. If you love space adventures and clever Lego builds, this set is a must-have. It's not the biggest, but it's definitely one of the most fun to play with.
why_it_matters: This set turns a movie’s science idea into something you can build and play with, showing that learning about space can be really creative and fun.

background_read: The movie 'Project Hail Mary' is based on a book by Andy Weir, the same author who wrote 'The Martian', another story about an astronaut alone in space.
In real science, spinning a spaceship can create a force that feels like gravity, called centrifugal force, which is what the Lego set shows.
Ryan Gosling (the famous actor who plays the astronaut) has starred in many popular films, including 'La La Land'.
Article_Structure: WHO: Lego released a set based on the movie with the characters Ryland and Rocky.
WHAT: A 830-piece spaceship model with a spinning crew section that mimics artificial gravity.
WHERE: The model sits on a display stand that hides the spinning mechanism.
WHY: To let kids build a fun, movie-accurate toy that moves like a real spaceship while showing a neat science idea.

perspectives.description: This is the coolest Lego because it actually spins like a real spaceship, making playtime feel like jumping into a sci-fi movie.
At $99.99 for 830 pieces, it costs more than some other sets, so kids might need to save up their allowance or ask for it as a special gift.
Having all the decorations printed on the bricks instead of stickers means the design will never peel off, which makes it great for collectors who want it to last.
